raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not toss things around too much. Five mu is not big, and our family still needs steady grain more than fancy ideas. I will still do wheat and maize, same as before. That way the land does not sit empty, and if one crop is not so good, the other still gives us something. I cannot read those technical papers, so I look at my own field and what people nearby are doing. If the wheat looked hungry last year, I give a bit more fertilizer. If water is costly, I do not water too many times, only at the important stages.

For wheat, I will sow in October like usual, not too early, not too late. I will use the seed we usually buy locally, the kind everybody knows, because I do not want trouble with poor emergence. Before sowing I will put on base fertilizer, then watch the color after winter. If the leaves turn pale at jointing, I will topdress again. Wheat cannot skip water here if I want a decent harvest, so I will irrigate a few times with the well, but not wastefully because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I will turn around quickly and plant maize right away. That window is short, so I keep tillage simple. For maize I do not spend as much on water unless the rain is poor. Fertilizer I still use, but a bit less than wheat. If weeds or insects show up badly, then I spray. I do not spray just for nothing. What I want is safe harvest, not the highest possible yield.
